## Purpose

This report compares the original `final_data.csv` with
`final_data_codex.csv`. Both files are read from `data/processed/` and are
compared on their structure, country-year coverage, and shared variables.

```{r}
#| label: setup
library(dplyr)
library(readr)
library(tidyr)

original_data <- read_csv("data/processed/final_data.csv", show_col_types = FALSE)
codex_data <- read_csv("data/processed/final_data_codex.csv", show_col_types = FALSE)

key_columns <- c("iso", "year")
```

## Data-set overview

The table below reports the number of rows, columns, and distinct country-year
observations in each file. A duplicate count of zero means that every row has a
unique `iso`-`year` combination.

```{r}
#| label: overview
overview <- bind_rows(
  original_data |> summarise(
    dataset = "final_data.csv",
    rows = n(),
    columns = ncol(original_data),
    unique_country_years = n_distinct(pick(all_of(key_columns))),
    duplicate_country_years = n() - n_distinct(pick(all_of(key_columns)))
  ),
  codex_data |> summarise(
    dataset = "final_data_codex.csv",
    rows = n(),
    columns = ncol(codex_data),
    unique_country_years = n_distinct(pick(all_of(key_columns))),
    duplicate_country_years = n() - n_distinct(pick(all_of(key_columns)))
  )
)

overview
```

## Variables present in each file

```{r}
#| label: variable-comparison
variable_comparison <- tibble(
  variable = union(names(original_data), names(codex_data)),
  in_final_data = variable %in% names(original_data),
  in_final_data_codex = variable %in% names(codex_data)
) |> arrange(variable)

variable_comparison
```

The original file retains `best` (the total battle-related deaths) and
`defined_conflict`; the Codex file instead retains the binary
`armed_conflict` variable. The remaining variables should be shared.

## Country-year coverage

```{r}
#| label: country-year-coverage
original_keys <- original_data |> distinct(across(all_of(key_columns)))
codex_keys <- codex_data |> distinct(across(all_of(key_columns)))

coverage_comparison <- tibble(
  comparison = c(
    "Country-years only in final_data.csv",
    "Country-years only in final_data_codex.csv",
    "Country-years in both files"
  ),
  n_country_years = c(
    nrow(anti_join(original_keys, codex_keys, by = key_columns)),
    nrow(anti_join(codex_keys, original_keys, by = key_columns)),
    nrow(inner_join(original_keys, codex_keys, by = key_columns))
  )
)

coverage_comparison
```

## Shared-variable values

For every variable found in both files, the next table counts matching and
non-matching values among country-years present in both files. Two missing
values are treated as a match.

```{r}
#| label: shared-values
shared_value_columns <- setdiff(
  intersect(names(original_data), names(codex_data)),
  key_columns
)

joined_data <- inner_join(
  original_data |> select(all_of(c(key_columns, shared_value_columns))),
  codex_data |> select(all_of(c(key_columns, shared_value_columns))),
  by = key_columns,
  suffix = c("_original", "_codex")
)

value_comparison <- lapply(shared_value_columns, function(variable) {
  original_value <- joined_data[[paste0(variable, "_original")]]
  codex_value <- joined_data[[paste0(variable, "_codex")]]
  matches <- (is.na(original_value) & is.na(codex_value)) |
    (!is.na(original_value) & !is.na(codex_value) & original_value == codex_value)

  tibble(
    variable = variable,
    matching_values = sum(matches),
    differing_values = sum(!matches)
  )
}) |> bind_rows() |> arrange(desc(differing_values), variable)

value_comparison
```

## Conclusion

Use `final_data_codex.csv` when the desired exposure is the explicitly named
binary `armed_conflict` variable. This report can be re-rendered whenever
either CSV is regenerated, so its tables will update automatically.
